The fix is complete. Here's a summary of what was wrong and what I changed.

## Root cause

In the moment-accumulation loops for skew/kurt, the code conflated two distinct notions of "missing": the boolean `mask` and a NaN float value. It did:

```cython
if uses_mask and mask[i]:
    val = NaN
if skipna and isnan(val):   # skips ANY NaN, even mask=False data
    continue
```

So when a `mask` was supplied, a genuine NaN sitting at a `mask=False` position was silently skipped instead of being treated as valid data. That's exactly the inconsistency you saw on grouped nullable float data.

## Fix

I made **`mask` the sole indicator of NA-ness whenever it is provided**, in three places (all Cython):

- `pandas/_libs/algos.pyx` — `accumulate_moments_scalar` (drives `nanskew`/`nankurt` for `axis=None`/`axis=0` scalar) and `accumulate_moments_axis` (drives `axis=0`/`axis=1`).
- `pandas/_libs/groupby.pyx` — `group_skew` and `group_kurt`.

The new logic:
```cython
if uses_mask:
    isna_entry = mask[i]          # NaN at mask=False is valid data
else:
    isna_entry = isnan(val)       # (+ _treat_as_na in groupby)
if isna_entry:
    if skipna:
        continue                  # only mask=True is skipped
    val = NaN                     # skipna=False: NA propagates to result
```

This gives the required semantics: with `skipna=True` only `mask=True` entries are skipped and `mask=False` NaNs propagate arithmetically; with `skipna=False` any `mask=True` entry forces a NaN result. The groupby result-mask handling (already present) then maps that to `pd.NA`/`np.nan` with `Float64` dtype.
